entities.summary:
Visual phenomenon where there is difficulty of seeing in presence of disturbance from a bright light. 

 The glare of intense sunlight or artificial illumination can cause discomfort and hinder vision, particularly in situations where the eyes are accustomed to lower light levels. 

 In various cultures, the effects of glare have been attributed to different causes, including the reflection of light from water or polished surfaces. 

 From an engineering perspective, glare is often addressed through the design of buildings, vehicles, and other structures to minimize the impact of bright lights on vision and visual comfort. 

 With the advent of modern lighting technologies and glare-reducing materials, the impact of glare on daily life has been significantly mitigated, although it still remains a consideration in many areas of human endeavor.

 As the Greek philosopher Aristotle noted, 'The eye is the window of the soul, but the glare of the sun can also be a window to the soul of humanity, revealing our capacity to adapt and innovate in the face of adversity.'
